QF.id: VB Concept and Role of Mutual Fund_17

question.text: What is a "unitholder" in a mutual fund?

answer.text: An investor who has purchased units of a mutual fund scheme
The fund manager who manages the scheme
The distributor who sells the mutual fund
The trustee who oversees the fund

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook, investors in a mutual fund scheme receive units in proportion to their investment and are called unit-holders. Unit-holders have rights to beneficial ownership of the underlying assets, and any profits or losses of the scheme accrue to them. The Trap: Fund managers, distributors, and trustees perform different roles in the mutual fund ecosystem. They are not, by virtue of those roles, unit-holders. Note: The workbook supports unit-holders as the beneficiaries who receive both the profits and the losses of the scheme.
